thread:
anya: Heads-up — ran into an odd parity issue between TS and Python SDKs in the starter tutorial. When using function-calling + json_mode with retries enabled, Python hands tools a quoted JSON string instead of a parsed object. New users hit TypeError in the sample app.

sam: Oof. Which versions and sample?

anya: py sdk 0.9.7, samplekit v0.6. Minimal repro in the quickstart: call 'register_user' via function_call while json_mode=True and retry enabled.

mohit: Can you paste the printed value you get?

anya: It prints: 
"\"{\"username\":\"anya\"}\""
(not a dict). TS SDK returns {"username":"anya"}.

tess: Sounds like the stream reassembler/security retry path is double-serializing. Does disabling retry make it behave?

anya: Yes, retry=False returns the dict. Only the retry path yields the quoted string.

sam: Short-term: update the onboarding doc with a defensive snippet — if isinstance(args, str): try json.loads(args) — and mention retry as a cause. Long-term: change coalescer so finalization attempts a single json.loads on string arguments and only json.dumps when dealing with bytes.

mohit: I'll open a PR with the patch + integration test for function_call + json_mode + retry parity with TS. Also add a changelog line.

ci-bot: Issue created #4310 (py-sdk): "fncall/json_mode: avoid double-encoding on retry". CI for branch fix/fncall-retry-parse queued.

anya: Thanks — I'll tweak the samplekit quickstart to include the workaround and link the issue for transparency. :thumbsup:
